question: Which statement best describes Flex container vs flex items?
options: Aligns items along the CROSS axis: stretch (default), flex-start, center, flex-end, baseline. center is half of the famous 'center anything' recipe (justify-content: center + align-items: center). align-self overrides it for one item.

Setting display: flex (or inline-flex) on an element turns it into a flex container; its direct children automatically become flex items. Container properties (justify-content, align-items, flex-direction) control layout of the group, while item properties (flex-grow, align-self, order) control individual children. Only direct children are flex items — grandchildren are not.

Distributes items along the MAIN axis: flex-start, center, flex-end, space-between (edges flush, gaps between), space-around, and space-evenly. It only has a visible effect when there's free space left over on the main axis. It's how you space out a navbar or center a single item horizontally (in a row).

Flexbox is built around two axes: the main axis (set by flex-direction) and the perpendicular cross axis. justify-content aligns items along the main axis; align-items aligns them along the cross axis. Flipping flex-direction from row to column swaps which axis each property controls — the #1 source of confusion.

The flex shorthand (flex: grow shrink basis) controls how items size along the main axis. flex-grow distributes extra space, flex-shrink lets items shrink when space is tight, and flex-basis is the starting size before growing/shrinking. flex: 1 (= 1 1 0) makes items share space equally — the basis of fluid layouts.
